_comment: Declarative on purpose. This file describes WHICH scraped labels mean what;
it contains no code, and it is interpreted server-side rather than in the
browser. A pack must never be able to ship JavaScript into a content script:
installing a pack would then mean granting it the ability to run on every
page the extension can see.
The extension's job shrinks to: collect label/value pairs off the page and
POST them. Which labels matter, and what they mean, lives here — so a new
listing site is a JSON file, and a site redesign is a data edit rather than
an extension release.

fuel._comment: The technical panel writes 'Gasoline / EURO 6' and, when the fuel row is absent, hides the fuel inside 'Motor Tipi' / 'Engine Type' ('Gasoline / 4 cylinders'). Both are the first segment.

transmission._comment: 'Şanzıman / Çekiş' reads 'Otomatik / Önden Çekiş'; the English panel reads 'DSG / 7 Gear / Front Wheel Drive'. The gearbox is the first segment in both.

power_min_hp._comment: 'Maksimum Güç' reads '110 hp (81 kw) / 4,600 rpm'; the range bound is what makes reading the first number safe — 81 and 4600 are both outside it.

build_year._comment: Falls back to the title. The info-list markup here has been redesigned repeatedly and every redesign zeroed every field; the year is the one identity key a title reliably carries.

derive._comment: Age is arithmetic on the build year, not a scraped field.

_comment: The panel the reader sees over their own page, declared rather than coded.
Everything here used to be JavaScript in extension/: the Turkish words that
name a damage state, the DOM selectors that find one, the English titles and
hints the panel prints, and the rules that turn a list of panels into a red
flag. All of it is site knowledge and category knowledge, and all of it had
the same failure mode the label lists had before Phase 6c — a site redesign,
or a second listing site, or a second category, meant an extension release.
It stays data, interpreted by a fixed evaluator, for the same reason the rest
of this file does: a pack that could ship JavaScript into a content script
would be a pack that runs code on every page the extension can see. Anything
this vocabulary cannot express is a reason to extend the evaluator once, in
review, rather than to open that door.
Term matching is folded on both sides (lowercase, accents stripped, dotless
i normalised), so 'degisen' here matches 'Değişen' on the page and an author
need not enumerate spellings.

legacy._comment: Older sahibinden DOMs encoded the state in CSS classes on the silhouette nodes themselves. Only read when the modern selectors above found nothing.

states._comment: Order is precedence: 'lokal boyalı' contains 'boyalı', so the narrower heading has to be tested first.
states.title: Replaced
states.hint: The panel was removed and a new one installed. Strong signal of serious prior damage; if the hood, roof or trunk lid is here, demand a chassis inspection.

states.title: Local paint
states.hint: Only a small area was repainted. Usually a minor scrape or stone-chip touch-up.

states.title: Painted
states.hint: The panel was resprayed. Panels are rarely repainted without a reason — usually an old impact or scratch repair. Check for colour mismatch and rust.

states._comment: Scraped, and deliberately given no title: an original panel is the absence of a finding, and a row of them would bury the three rows that are findings. The alert rules below still read it.

measures.title: Damage claim
measures.hint: Insurance-recorded damage amount. The larger the figure, the more serious the past repair.

alerts.say: Hood replaced: likely severe frontal collision. Have an expert inspect the chassis rails and engine mounts.
Roof replaced: possible rollover or major impact. A-pillars and chassis alignment must be checked.
Trunk lid replaced: likely serious rear impact. Inspect rear chassis members and the rear floor.
{n} panels replaced on the same side: likely side-impact collision. Have an expert check pillars and chassis straightness.

alerts._comment: `unless` is how an else-branch is written without giving the format a control flow: the broad rule stays quiet when the specific one already spoke.
alerts.say: {n} panels replaced overall: significant repair history. Do not buy without a full pre-purchase inspection.

alerts._comment: A painted panel that was also replaced says nothing extra — the replacement alert already fired and is the worse news.
alerts.say: Roof painted: roofs are rarely repainted without a real cause. Check pillars and chassis alignment.
Hood painted: possible front impact or scratch repair. Verify engine mounts, headlight fit and colour match.
Trunk lid painted: possible rear impact repair. Check rear cross-member and trunk seal alignment.
Painted panels on both sides (left: {left}, right: {right}): likely multiple impacts or extensive cosmetic refinishing.
{n} panels painted overall: a large portion of the car has been refinished. Inspect for colour mismatch, rust, and hidden damage.
High insurance claim recorded ({value} {currency}): significant past damage. Request the full Tramer history report.

_ignore_comment: These labels are not read at all, not merely left out of the coverage
report. Several of them are near-misses for a rule above — 'Yakıt
Tüketimi' contains 'yakıt', 'Motor Tipi' contains 'motor' — and the
extension no longer filters anything client-side, so this list is the
only thing that stops a consumption figure being read as a fuel type.
